app.name: Subduction State
app.tagline: Global observatory of loaded-but-quiet subduction regimes
app.disclaimer: Experimental geophysical research interface. Regime scores are not earthquake predictions or official hazard warnings. Follow local geological and civil-defense authorities for emergency information.

couplingAsperity.name: Megathrust coupling
couplingAsperity.description: Geodetic locking of the plate interface and the coherence of strongly coupled patches.

slipDeficitMaturity.name: Slip deficit
slipDeficitMaturity.description: How far the segment has progressed through its seismic cycle — a cycle-maturity feature, never 'percent toward failure'.

longTermQuiescence.name: Long-term gap
longTermQuiescence.description: Long-duration absence of segment-scale great ruptures over a highly coupled zone.

recentQuiescence.name: Recent quiescence
recentQuiescence.description: Recent M4+ activity suppressed relative to this region's own historical baseline.

interfaceActivation.name: Interface activation
interfaceActivation.description: Activity around asperity edges and segment boundaries while the locked interior stays quiet.

gnssTransient.name: GNSS transient
gnssTransient.description: Recent deviation of processed GNSS positions from each station's own trend and scatter.

environmentalPerturbation.name: Environment
environmentalPerturbation.description: Local SST and sea-level anomalies plus ENSO context — deliberately low weight, unvalidated causal value.

remotePerturbation.name: Remote events
remotePerturbation.description: Experimental proxy for recent large earthquakes nearby. Not Coulomb stress transfer.

volcanicResponse.name: Volcanic response
volcanicResponse.description: Newly started eruptions within 500 km. Pre-existing activity contributes nothing.

alongMarginMigration.name: Migration
alongMarginMigration.description: Whether independent earthquakes progress consistently along the margin over time.

methodology.title: Methodology & scientific limitations
methodology.intro: Subduction State measures how strongly the currently observed conditions of a subduction segment resemble a hypothesised regime: high structural loading, accumulated deformation, relative seismic quiet, and possible external perturbation. It is a similarity metric over observable data. It is not, and cannot be, an earthquake forecast.

what.title: What the score measures
what.body: The Loaded–Quiet Megathrust Regime Score aggregates ten weighted variables (below). Each variable is scored 0–100 from live, derived, curated or experimental evidence, or is null when unknown. The primary number you see is the observed-data score: known contributions renormalised over the known weight. Alongside it you always see data coverage and the full possible-score interval, because unknown ≠ normal.
what.structural: Structural variables exist for every region: coupling is a cited literature prior per segment; slip deficit and long-term gap are computed from the public great-rupture record (USGS/NEIC, NOAA), the MORVEL convergence rate and that prior. Partial ruptures do not reset the full-segment deficit; regions with no recorded segment-scale great rupture honestly show unknown.

not.title: What it does NOT measure
items: It is not an earthquake probability.
It is not a rupture probability for any fault.
It is not 'percent toward failure' — the slip-deficit component is a cycle-maturity feature, not a countdown.
It is not a calibrated statistical forecast of any kind.
It is not an official warning, alert or product of any civil-defense or geological agency.

weights.title: Canonical V0.1 weights
weights.note: Local geodetic and structural measurements dominate; environmental and remote-event proxies are deliberately low-weight because their causal earthquake-predictive value is unvalidated.

math.title: Score mathematics
math.note: The neutral-imputed value exists for research tooling and backtesting. It is never the primary displayed score.

missing.title: Why missing data create ranges
missing.body: A variable with no trustworthy data contributes nothing and is excluded from the denominator. A region can therefore be honest about what it does not know: 71 observed over 80% coverage means the full score could lie anywhere in a 16-point interval. Missing GNSS never becomes GNSS = 0.

comparison.title: Why regional comparisons are difficult
comparison.body: Data completeness varies enormously between subduction margins. A region scoring 85 with 30% coverage should be read as less authoritative than a region scoring 65 with 95% coverage, and the interface enforces this visually. Never compare scores without comparing coverage.

correlation.title: Why correlation does not imply triggering
correlation.body: Remote earthquakes, climate anomalies and volcanic activity may coincide with local regimes without any causal relationship. The remote-perturbation variable is a geometric/time-decay proxy — it is explicitly not Coulomb stress transfer. Environmental variables carry ≤ 5% weight precisely because their causal value is unvalidated. Nothing in this interface claims that any anomaly causes earthquakes.

declustering.title: Declustering (ETAS-lite)
declustering.body: Quiescence, activation and migration statistics use a transparent aftershock heuristic: events within a magnitude-dependent radius (≈10^(0.5M−1.4) km) and time window (≈10^(0.55M−1.95) d) of a prior M6+ event are flagged as aftershock candidates. This is not a full ETAS model and does not estimate triggering probabilities.

provenance.title: Reproducibility & provenance
provenance.body: Every score opens an evidence drawer with the raw value, the transformation, the formula, the source, its freshness and confidence. Curated structural priors cite their publications and review dates. If a number cannot be traced, it does not belong in this interface.

future.title: Known gaps
items: GNSS coverage depends on public processed time series (UNR NGL); many segments have too few current stations — the metric stays unknown rather than guessed.
GEM active-fault geometry requires a configured export URL; it is map context, never a hazard model.
Volcanic 'new activity' relies on GVP eruption-onset years, which are approximate and back-filled.
Historical replay currently covers seismic-derived metrics only; GNSS/environmental history is not fabricated.
Along-margin migration is experimental and requires ≥4 independent clusters.

data.title: Data sources, freshness & API health
data.subtitle: Every adapter records its last fetch and observation. Failures fall back to labeled caches — never to silent fabrication.
attribution: Earthquake data: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) ComCat, public domain.
Volcano data: Smithsonian Institution, Global Volcanism Program (VOTW).
SST anomaly & sea-level anomaly: NOAA CoastWatch / Coral Reef Watch (ERDDAP).
GNSS: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory, University of Nevada, Reno.
Fault geometry (optional layer): GEM Global Active Faults Database (CC-BY-SA).
Basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors, tiles by OpenFreeMap.
data.gemNote: The GEM active-faults layer is disabled until a GAF-DB export is configured via GEM_GAF_URL. Fault geometry would be used as visual context only.

research.title: Research mode
research.subtitle: Experimental re-weighting of the scoring framework. Changes are local to your browser and always visible.
research.customActiveNote: Scores shown across the app use your custom weights. The methodology V0.1 canonical weights remain the reference.
research.disableMetric: Disable (redistributes nothing — the variable drops from coverage)
research.importInvalid: Invalid configuration — weights must sum to 100 and values must be in range.
research.livePreviewNote: Recomputed instantly from cached metric scores — dynamic metrics use the server's canonical windows; custom windows mark the display as indicative.
research.noteServer: Custom thresholds/windows affect display aggregation. Server-side metrics are always recomputed canonically for reproducibility.

footer.builtAs: Built as an experimental research framework for regime characterization.
